subject.title: fix: inject only shared auth into macos dashboard

question: Should the embedded macOS Dashboard browser ever receive native device/operator tokens, or must browser injection be limited to configured shared gateway token/password auth?
rationale: This PR and https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/98473 intentionally choose opposite credential boundaries for the same Dashboard auth surface, and current main added another reload path that must follow whichever policy maintainers select.

options.title: Use shared-token-only browser injection
options.body: Proceed with this PR's security boundary, rebase it over current main, update the endpoint-reload path, and require macOS proof before merge.

options.title: Use native-token parity
options.body: Close or pause this PR and continue with the sibling parity approach that lets native/operator tokens authenticate the embedded Dashboard browser.

options.title: Defer until auth design is documented
options.body: Keep both draft PRs paused while maintainers document the Dashboard browser/native credential contract and upgrade behavior.

recommendation.title: Use shared-token-only browser injection
recommendation.body: Proceed with this PR's security boundary, rebase it over current main, update the endpoint-reload path, and require macOS proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete authored the native Dashboard window and the current endpoint-reload work that now needs to be reconciled with this auth policy.
